title: Intersection of Two Arrays
statement: You get two integer arrays `nums1` and `nums2`. Return a list of the values that occur in both arrays, listing each such value only once even if it repeats in either input. The values may be returned in any order; if the arrays share no value, return an empty list.
notes:
## Intuition

Comparing every value of one array with every value of the other works but costs O(n · m), and it still has to skip repeats in the answer. A set answers "is this value in `nums1`?" in constant time, and removing a value from the set once it is reported makes sure no value is reported twice.

## Approach

1. Put every value of `nums1` into a set `seen`; duplicates collapse automatically.
2. Walk through `nums2` one `num` at a time.
3. If `num` is in `seen`, it is common to both arrays: append it to `result`.
4. Delete it from `seen` right away, so later copies of `num` in `nums2` are ignored.
5. Return `result`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums1 = [1, 2, 2, 1]` gives `seen = {1, 2}`. The first `2` of `nums2` is in `seen`, so `result = [2]` and `seen` becomes `{1}`. The second `2` is no longer in `seen` and is skipped. The answer is `[2]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + m): building the set and scanning `nums2` are each linear.
- Space: O(n) for the set (the output holds at most min(n, m) values).

## Pitfalls

- Report each common value once: without the `delete`, `[1, 2, 2, 1]` and `[2, 2]` would give `[2, 2]`.
- The answer may be empty, which is a valid result, not an error.
- The order of the output does not matter, so do not spend time sorting it.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `seen` | values of `nums1` not yet reported |
| `result` | common values found so far |
| `num` | the current value of `nums2` |

narration.2: Load nums1 into a set; repeated values are stored once.
narration.3: result will collect each common value exactly once.
narration.5: Scan the second array value by value.
narration.6: Is this value also present in nums1 (and not reported yet)?
narration.7: Yes: it belongs to the intersection.
narration.8: Remove it so later copies in nums2 are not reported again.
narration.11: Every value of nums2 has been checked; return the common values.
